messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmeretail.com>, Sam Collins <sam.collins@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-25T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Time-to-first-token preflight & streaming requirements — contract preflight

Hi Julia / Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a narrow set of asks so we can scope a pilot and draft terms: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct anything):
- Primary goal: <user-facing chat product> with tight interactive feel. TTFT is the critical metric.
- Target TTFT (first token) outcomes: aiming for sub-150ms median for short prompts (user messages ~20-60 tokens), and 95th percentile target in the 250–350ms range depending on payload.
- Peak concurrency: ~2,500 concurrent chat sessions in US region at launch; steady-state 800–1,000.
- Throughput mix: 60% short-turn chats (prompt+short reply), 40% longer generation sessions (200–400 tokens).
- Streaming behavior: prefer WebSocket; fallback to SSE if websockets are blocked. Need per-chunk arrival cadence <=200ms for perceived fluidity, and a heartbeat every 5–10s to keep connections alive.
- Security: no cross-customer KV-caching; we’ll need assurance on data separation and audit logs.

Immediate asks for us to size and price the pilot: 
1) Can you confirm a hard TTFT target to commit to for pilot acceptance (we used sub-150ms median / 95th <350ms as a starting point)?
2) Confirm expected concurrency profile (peak vs steady) and any scheduled bursts (marketing events).
3) Are there networking constraints (strict corporate proxies) that would force SSE-only?
4) Any compliance items we should include in the pilot SOO (SOC 2 evidence, region restrictions)?

Attachments: I attached a short SLO draft and a one-page timeline we discussed.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm answers to the 4 asks above by EOD tomorrow.
- We schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive with our runtime engineers to validate protocol choices and load tests (suggest Wed 28 Jul, 11am PT).
- If SLOs align, we'll run a 2-week pilot with measurement harness and agreed acceptance criteria.

If this matches your view, I’ll have Ben and Priyom put together a capacity estimate and initial pricing.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmeretail.com>

Date: 2027-07-25T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Time-to-first-token preflight & streaming requirements — contract preflight

Thanks Rachel — great summary. A few clarifications from our side and some firm numbers: 

Confirmed needs / constraints:
- TTFT targets: for the customer-facing product we need median first-token <=140ms for the 20–80 token prompt range. 95th should be <=320ms for the pilot; long-form sessions can relax to 500ms 95th.
- Concurrency: peak ~2.5k concurrent, but 90% of the time we expect 700–1,000. We do have two weekly marketing spikes that could double peak for 5–10 minutes; will share exact times after internal calendar check.
- Chunk cadence: our UX team observed that chunk gaps >200ms feel choppy. We want the first chunk within 120–150ms where possible and subsequent chunks every 100–200ms depending on generation rate.
- Protocol: prefer WebSocket (bi-directional routing for quick user edits). Some enterprise customers sit behind strict proxies; SSE fallback required.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II evidence is required; also need per-token logging for audit (we can redact content) and region restriction to US only for pilot.

Attachments: I uploaded an annotated SLO draft with examples of user scenarios (see attached).

We can do Wed 28 Jul for the technical deep-dive; 11am PT works for Sam and me. Please include engineers who own the SSE/WebSocket stack and a runtime engineer who can speak to KV cache behavior.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Head of Product — Conversational Experiences, Acme Retail
[attachment: acme_slo_draft_v2.pdf]

Looping in Priyom to size and give a capacity/price sketch. Quick initial notes based on Julia’s numbers: 

Feasibility notes:
- TTFT median <140ms + 95th <320ms at 2.5k peak is achievable with Dedicated pools (pinned GPUs) and careful batching. We’d recommend a Dedicated pilot to get predictable tail latency; hosted variable capacity could struggle with the 95th percentile during marketing spikes.
- Streaming: WebSocket preferred — our runtime supports both. We can tune chunk flush windows and adjust tokenization thresholds to hit the 120–150ms first-chunk goal for short responses.
- Caching: we’ll honor no cross-tenant KV caching; that adds tokens cost but is fine for pilot.

Pilot sizing ask list for Priyom: 
1) Pilot capacity: size for 3k concurrent with headroom (to cover spikes).
2) Baseline test plan: 48-hour soak with synthetic traffic (mix: 60% short-turn, 40% long-form).
3) Acceptance metrics: median TTFT, 95th TTFT, live threading latency, chunk cadence distribution, connection drop rate.
4) Estimate cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated pilot.

I attached a quick CSV timeline we can use to propose dates (pilot start, load test windows). Priyom — can you return initial numbers by EOD tomorrow? I’ll draft an annotated SOW once we have sizing.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
